problem.title: String Word Frequency Counter
problem.description: Implement a function that counts how many times each word appears in a given string, ignoring case and punctuation.
requirements: Return an object where keys are lowercase words and values are their occurrence counts
Treat words case-insensitively so 'Hello' and 'hello' count as the same word
Strip common punctuation (period, comma, exclamation mark, question mark) from words before counting
Return an empty object for an empty string or whitespace-only input
Handle multiple spaces between words gracefully
Words separated only by punctuation (e.g. 'dog,cat') should be treated as separate words only if a space or punctuation boundary exists
hints: Use String.prototype.toLowerCase() early in your pipeline before splitting
Consider using a regular expression like /[.,!?]/g with String.prototype.replace() to strip punctuation before splitting on spaces

problem.title: Temperature Unit Converter
problem.description: Implement a converter that transforms temperature values between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin units. Results should be accurate and handle invalid inputs gracefully.
requirements: Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit using the formula F = (C × 9/5) + 32
Convert Fahrenheit to Celsius using the formula C = (F − 32) × 5/9
Convert Celsius to Kelvin using the formula K = C + 273.15
Round all results to 2 decimal places
Throw an error when a temperature below absolute zero (−273.15°C or 0K or −459.67°F) is provided as input
hints: Start by writing a test for the simplest case (0°C = 32°F) and make it pass before adding more conversions
For rounding, use Math.round(value * 100) / 100 or toFixed(2) — consider where in the formula to apply it to avoid floating-point drift

problem.title: Mathematical Expression Parser with Variables
problem.description: Implement a recursive descent parser that tokenizes, parses, and evaluates arithmetic expressions. The parser must support named variables, correct operator precedence, parentheses, unary operators, and right-associative exponentiation.
requirements: Evaluate binary expressions (+, -, *, /) with correct operator precedence: multiplication and division bind tighter than addition and subtraction
Support parenthesized sub-expressions that override default precedence (e.g., '(2 + 3) * 4' evaluates to 20)
Support named variable placeholders resolved via an environment map at evaluation time (e.g., evaluate('x * y', { x: 3, y: 4 }) returns 12)
Handle the unary minus operator applied to numbers, variables, and parenthesized groups (e.g., '-x', '-(x + 1)')
Support right-associative exponentiation via the ^ operator so that '2^3^2' evaluates as '2^(3^2)' = 512, not '(2^3)^2' = 64
Throw a descriptive Error for malformed input: unmatched parentheses, unknown variables, division by zero, or consecutive binary operators
hints: Structure the parser as a recursive descent with one function per precedence level — parseExpr (+ / -) calls parseTerm (* /) which calls parsePower (^) which calls parseUnary (negation) which calls parsePrimary (literals, variables, parenthesized groups). The call chain enforces precedence without any explicit table.

For right-associativity of ^, resist the usual while-loop pattern: instead of looping left-to-right inside parsePower, make a single recursive call back to parsePower for the right operand. This naturally produces a right-leaning parse tree.

problem.title: Recursive Descent Expression Parser with Variables
problem.description: Implement a parser and evaluator for arithmetic expressions that supports operator precedence, parentheses, and named variables resolved from a context map.
requirements: Parse and evaluate expressions containing integer/float literals with +, -, *, / operators respecting standard precedence (multiplication and division before addition and subtraction)
Support parentheses for explicit grouping, allowing arbitrary nesting depth
Resolve named variable identifiers (e.g. `x`, `totalCount`) from a provided context Record<string, number>; throw a ReferenceError if a variable is not found in the context
Support unary minus on both literals and parenthesised sub-expressions (e.g. `-3`, `-(x + 1)`)
Throw a SyntaxError with a descriptive message when the input contains unbalanced parentheses, unknown tokens, or is otherwise malformed
Return an exact number (IEEE 754 double) matching JavaScript's native arithmetic semantics for the same expression
hints: Model the parser as three mutually-recursive functions — parseExpression (handles + and -), parseTerm (handles * and /), parsePrimary (handles literals, variables, unary minus, and parenthesised groups) — this directly encodes operator precedence without any precedence-climbing algorithm

Tokenise the input string first into a flat array of typed tokens (NUMBER, IDENT, PLUS, MINUS, STAR, SLASH, LPAREN, RPAREN, EOF) and advance through it with a cursor index; separating lexing from parsing makes each stage independently testable

problem.title: Shopping Basket with Discount Rules
problem.description: Implement a shopping basket that tracks items and applies configurable discount rules to calculate the final total. Support both percentage-off discounts and buy-N-get-M-free promotions.
requirements: Add items to the basket with a name, unit price, and quantity; retrieve the subtotal (sum of price × quantity for all items)
Apply a percentage discount to the entire basket (e.g., 10% off) and return the discounted total rounded to 2 decimal places
Apply a 'buy N get M free' promotion to a specific item (e.g., buy 2 get 1 free on apples reduces the charged quantity accordingly)
Multiple discount rules can be registered and all are applied when calculating the final total; percentage discount applies after buy-N-get-M savings
Raise a ValueError when adding an item with a non-positive price or quantity, or when a discount percentage is not between 0 and 100 exclusive
problem.exampleTest:
from basket import Basket

def test_subtotal_without_discounts():
    b = Basket()
    b.add_item('apple', price=0.50, quantity=6)
    b.add_item('bread', price=1.20, quantity=2)
    assert b.subtotal() == 5.40

def test_percentage_discount():
    b = Basket()
    b.add_item('apple', price=1.00, quantity=10)
    b.add_percentage_discount(10)  # 10% off
    assert b.total() == 9.00

def test_buy_n_get_m_free():
    b = Basket()
    b.add_item('apple', price=0.50, quantity=6)
    b.add_bogo('apple', buy=2, free=1)  # buy 2 get 1 free → charged for 4
    assert b.total() == 2.00

def test_combined_discounts():
    b = Basket()
    b.add_item('cola', price=1.00, quantity=3)
    b.add_bogo('cola', buy=2, free=1)  # charged for 2 → subtotal 2.00
    b.add_percentage_discount(50)       # then 50% off → 1.00
    assert b.total() == 1.00

def test_invalid_price_raises():
    b = Basket()
    try:
        b.add_item('ghost', price=0, quantity=1)
        assert False, 'Expected ValueError'
    except ValueError:
        pass
hints: Model each item as a dataclass or namedtuple; store promotions as a list of rule objects or callables so new discount types can be added without changing the core calculation logic
For buy-N-get-M-free, compute charged_quantity = quantity - (quantity // (buy + free)) * free before multiplying by unit price; apply this per-item before summing the basket total

problem.title: Bank Account Transaction Ledger
problem.description: Implement a bank account class that tracks deposits, withdrawals, and maintains a transaction history with balance snapshots. The account must enforce business rules such as overdraft prevention and minimum balance requirements.
requirements: Deposit a positive amount and reflect it in the balance immediately
Withdraw an amount only if sufficient funds exist; raise an exception (e.g. InsufficientFundsError) otherwise
Return the full transaction history as a list of dicts with keys 'type', 'amount', and 'balance_after'
Support a minimum balance threshold set at account creation; withdrawals that would drop below it must be rejected
Return the net total of all deposits minus all withdrawals via a `net_flow()` method
Reset the account to its initial state (zero balance, empty history) via a `reset()` method
problem.exampleTest:
import pytest

class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    pass

# Assume BankAccount is imported from solution module

def test_deposit_increases_balance():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=0)
    account.deposit(100)
    assert account.balance == 100

def test_withdrawal_decreases_balance():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=0)
    account.deposit(200)
    account.withdraw(50)
    assert account.balance == 150

def test_overdraft_raises_error():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=0)
    account.deposit(30)
    with pytest.raises(InsufficientFundsError):
        account.withdraw(100)

def test_minimum_balance_enforced():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=50)
    account.deposit(100)
    with pytest.raises(InsufficientFundsError):
        account.withdraw(60)  # would leave 40, below minimum of 50

def test_transaction_history():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=0)
    account.deposit(100)
    account.withdraw(40)
    history = account.transaction_history()
    assert history == [
        {'type': 'deposit', 'amount': 100, 'balance_after': 100},
        {'type': 'withdrawal', 'amount': 40, 'balance_after': 60},
    ]

def test_net_flow():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=0)
    account.deposit(200)
    account.withdraw(80)
    account.deposit(50)
    assert account.net_flow() == 170  # 250 deposited - 80 withdrawn

def test_reset_clears_state():
    account = BankAccount(minimum_balance=0)
    account.deposit(500)
    account.reset()
    assert account.balance == 0
    assert account.transaction_history() == []
hints: Store transactions as a list of dicts internally and derive `balance` and `net_flow()` from it, or maintain them as separate tracked attributes — choose one strategy and stay consistent
Define `InsufficientFundsError` as a custom exception subclassing `Exception`; check both zero-balance overdraft and minimum-balance violations in the same guard clause inside `withdraw()`

problem.title: Caesar Cipher Encoder and Decoder
problem.description: Implement a Caesar cipher that encodes and decodes strings by shifting each alphabetic character by a given number of positions. Non-alphabetic characters must pass through unchanged.
requirements: Encode a string by shifting each lowercase letter forward by N positions (e.g., 'a' with shift 3 becomes 'd')
Encode a string by shifting each uppercase letter forward by N positions, preserving case (e.g., 'A' with shift 3 becomes 'D')
Letters that go past 'z' or 'Z' must wrap around to the beginning (e.g., 'z' with shift 1 becomes 'a')
Non-alphabetic characters such as digits, spaces, and punctuation must remain unchanged
Decode a string by applying the inverse shift, exactly recovering the original input
A shift of 0 or any multiple of 26 must return the original string unchanged
hints: Use Go's rune type to iterate over the string; check if a rune falls between 'a'-'z' or 'A'-'Z' before applying the shift
Wrap-around can be handled with modulo arithmetic: shifted = (char - base + shift) % 26 + base, where base is 'a' or 'A'

problem.title: FizzBuzz with Custom Rules
problem.description: Implement a FizzBuzz function that returns a string slice for a given range, replacing multiples of 3 with 'Fizz', multiples of 5 with 'Buzz', and multiples of both with 'FizzBuzz'.
requirements: Return 'Fizz' for numbers divisible by 3
Return 'Buzz' for numbers divisible by 5
Return 'FizzBuzz' for numbers divisible by both 3 and 5
Return the number as a string for all other values
Accept a start and end integer (inclusive) and return a []string of results
Return an empty slice when start is greater than end
hints: Use the modulo operator (%) to check divisibility; check for divisibility by 15 (3×5) before checking 3 or 5 individually to avoid incorrect output.
Use fmt.Sprintf("%d", n) or strconv.Itoa(n) to convert integers to strings for the default case.

problem.title: Shopping Cart with Tiered Discounts
problem.description: Implement a shopping cart that calculates totals and applies tiered discount rules based on item count and order value. The cart must support adding/removing items and applying promotional codes.
requirements: Adding an item with a name and price stores it in the cart; getTotal() returns the sum of all item prices
Removing an item by name removes the first matching item; removing a non-existent item leaves the cart unchanged
Orders with 3 or more items receive a 10% discount; orders with 5 or more items receive a 20% discount (discounts do not stack)
Applying promo code 'SAVE5' subtracts a flat 5.0 from the total after quantity discounts; applying an invalid code throws IllegalArgumentException
getItemCount() returns the total number of items currently in the cart
clear() removes all items and resets any applied promo code; getTotal() then returns 0.0
hints: Store items in a List<Item> where Item is a simple record or inner class holding name and price; apply discount tiers in getTotal() by checking list size before summing
Track the promo code as a nullable field and subtract its value after the quantity discount in getTotal(); validate the code in applyPromoCode() and throw immediately if unrecognised

problem.title: Bank Account with Transaction History
problem.description: Implement a bank account that supports deposits, withdrawals, and produces a formatted transaction history statement. The account must enforce a minimum balance and track all operations with running balance.
requirements: Deposit a positive amount to increase the account balance; throw IllegalArgumentException for zero or negative amounts
Withdraw a positive amount that does not exceed the current balance; throw IllegalStateException if funds are insufficient, and IllegalArgumentException for non-positive amounts
Maintain an ordered list of transactions, each recording the type (DEPOSIT or WITHDRAWAL), amount, and resulting balance after the operation
Return a formatted statement string where each line follows the pattern: 'DEPOSIT 500.00 | Balance: 1500.00' or 'WITHDRAWAL 200.00 | Balance: 1300.00'
Return the current balance accurately after any sequence of deposits and withdrawals
Support querying total deposited and total withdrawn amounts as separate values
hints: Model each transaction as a simple record or inner class with fields: type (enum), amount, and balanceAfter — this makes statement formatting straightforward
Use String.format('%.2f', amount) to produce consistently formatted decimal values in the statement output

problem.title: Shopping Cart Discount Calculator
problem.description: Build a shopping cart system that calculates totals and applies discount rules based on cart value and product categories. Implement methods to add items, compute subtotals, apply discounts, and return the final price.
requirements: Add items to cart with quantity, price per unit, and category; store them for later retrieval
Calculate cart subtotal by summing (quantity × price) for all items
Apply percentage discount to specific product categories (e.g., electronics 5% off)
Apply percentage discount if subtotal exceeds a threshold amount (e.g., 10% off for orders over $50)
Return an object containing subtotal, total discount amount, and final price after all discounts
Handle empty carts and ensure final price never becomes negative
hints: Start by writing a test for addItem and creating a data structure to store cart items
Implement calculateTotal first for subtotals only, then layer on category discounts, then threshold discounts
Apply discounts in a consistent order (category discounts first, then threshold) to keep tests predictable
Test edge cases early: empty cart, single item, multiple discounts stacking, and threshold boundaries

problem.title: Email Validator and Normalizer
problem.description: Implement an email validator that checks basic email format rules (local@domain.tld structure) and provides a normalizer to convert emails to lowercase.
requirements: Validate that an email contains exactly one @ symbol
Validate that the local part (before @) is not empty
Validate that the domain part (after @) contains at least one dot
Validate that the TLD (part after the last dot) is 2-6 characters long
Provide a normalize method that converts the email to lowercase
hints: Use split('@') to separate the local and domain parts
To ensure exactly one @, check that the split result has exactly 2 elements
Find the last dot in the domain using lastIndexOf('.')
The TLD is the substring after the last dot
Use toLowerCase() for normalization

problem.title: Expression Evaluator with Functions and Precedence
problem.description: Implement a mathematical expression evaluator supporting arithmetic operations, operator precedence, parentheses, variables, and user-defined functions. Handle edge cases including nested calls, division by zero, and undefined identifiers.
requirements: Parse and evaluate arithmetic expressions (+, -, *, /) with correct operator precedence (* and / before + and -)
Support parentheses for grouping and enforce correct order of operations
Substitute variables from a provided context object; throw error for undefined variables
Support user-defined functions with parameters via defineFunction(name, params, body) and evaluate function calls in expressions
Throw descriptive errors for invalid expressions, division by zero, undefined variables, and undefined functions
Handle edge cases: negative numbers, whitespace, nested function calls, and multi-digit numbers
hints: Use the Shunting Yard algorithm or recursive descent parser to handle operator precedence and parentheses correctly
Separate concerns: tokenization (breaking input into tokens) from evaluation (parsing and computing results)
Store function definitions in a Map with parameter names and expression bodies; use string replacement or a symbol table for parameters
Implement recursive evaluation for nested expressions and function calls
Build incrementally with TDD: start with numbers and operators, add precedence, then parentheses, variables, and finally functions

problem.title: JSON Schema Validator with Custom Rules
problem.description: Implement a JSON Schema validator that validates data against schemas with custom predicates and reports detailed errors with JSON paths to problematic fields.
requirements: Support type validation for primitive types (string, number, boolean, null) and container types (array, object)
Validate string constraints (minLength, maxLength, pattern with regex) and number constraints (minimum, maximum, enum)
Validate required fields in objects and enforce itemSchema validation for all array elements
Report validation errors with JSON path to the invalid field (e.g., 'user.profile.zipcode') and failure reason
Support custom validation predicates as composable functions that can be added to any field schema
Handle deeply nested and circular object structures without stack overflow or infinite loops
problem.exampleTest: const userSchema = { type: 'object', required: ['name', 'email'], properties: { name: { type: 'string', minLength: 1 }, email: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[^@]+@[^@]+$' }, age: { type: 'number', minimum: 0, maximum: 150 } } }; const valid = { name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@example.com', age: 30 }; expect(validate(valid, userSchema)).toEqual([]); const invalid = { name: '', email: 'invalid' }; const errors = validate(invalid, userSchema); expect(errors.length).toBeGreaterThan(0); expect(errors.some(e => e.path === 'name')).toBe(true); expect(errors.some(e => e.path === 'email')).toBe(true);
hints: Start with basic type validation before adding constraint checking and nested structure support
Use a recursive validator function that tracks the current JSON path as it traverses the data structure
Separate validation logic into independent functions for each constraint type to keep code modular
Design a custom error object that captures path, failure reason, and schema context for detailed reporting

problem.title: Shopping Cart with Discounts and Tax
problem.description: Implement a shopping cart system that can add items, apply discounts and coupons, calculate taxes, and generate the final total.
requirements: Add items to cart with name, price, and quantity; handle duplicate items by updating quantity
Calculate subtotal of all items in cart (sum of price × quantity for each item)
Apply member discount as a percentage (e.g., 10% off subtotal)
Apply coupon code for a fixed amount discount
Calculate sales tax based on subtotal after all discounts are applied
Calculate and return final total (subtotal - discounts + tax); support getting total with custom tax rate
problem.exampleTest:
def test_add_item():
    cart = ShoppingCart()
    cart.add_item('Apple', 1.50, 3)
    assert cart.get_subtotal() == 4.50

def test_apply_member_discount():
    cart = ShoppingCart()
    cart.add_item('Milk', 3.00, 2)
    cart.apply_member_discount(0.10)
    assert cart.get_total(tax_rate=0.0) == 5.40

def test_apply_coupon():
    cart = ShoppingCart()
    cart.add_item('Bread', 2.00, 1)
    cart.apply_coupon(0.50)
    assert cart.get_total(tax_rate=0.0) == 1.50

def test_calculate_total_with_tax():
    cart = ShoppingCart()
    cart.add_item('Cheese', 5.00, 1)
    assert cart.get_total(tax_rate=0.08) == 5.40
hints: Use a list or dictionary to store cart items with their name, price, and quantity
Calculate in order: subtotal → apply member discount → apply coupon → add tax
When adding a duplicate item, decide whether to update quantity or store separately
Keep member discount and coupon as separate instance attributes so they accumulate
Handle edge cases: empty cart, zero discount/coupon, negative quantities, tax rate as decimal

problem.title: Inventory Management System
problem.description: Implement an inventory tracking system that manages product stock levels, handles restocking, and detects when items are running low. Support querying current inventory status and calculating total inventory value.
requirements: Create an Inventory class with add_product(sku, unit_price, reorder_level) to register a new product
Implement add_stock(sku, quantity) to increase inventory for a product
Implement remove_stock(sku, quantity) to decrease inventory; raise ValueError if insufficient stock exists
Implement is_low_stock(sku) that returns True if current quantity is at or below the reorder level
Implement get_total_value() that calculates total inventory value as the sum of (quantity × unit_price) for all products
Raise appropriate exceptions for invalid operations: duplicate SKUs, negative quantities, missing products, and non-positive unit prices
problem.exampleTest:
from inventory import Inventory

inv = Inventory()
inv.add_product('WIDGET-001', unit_price=9.99, reorder_level=10)
inv.add_stock('WIDGET-001', 50)
assert inv.get_quantity('WIDGET-001') == 50
assert not inv.is_low_stock('WIDGET-001')

inv.remove_stock('WIDGET-001', 45)
assert inv.get_quantity('WIDGET-001') == 5
assert inv.is_low_stock('WIDGET-001')
assert abs(inv.get_total_value() - 49.95) < 0.01

try:
    inv.remove_stock('WIDGET-001', 10)
    assert False, 'Should raise ValueError'
except ValueError:
    pass
hints: Start with add_product and get_quantity; implement and test these core methods before adding complexity
Store products in a dictionary using SKU as the key; each value should hold price, quantity, and reorder_level
For remove_stock, validate sufficient stock exists before modifying state; fail fast with a clear error message
Use floating-point comparison with a small epsilon (like 0.01) when testing get_total_value() due to currency rounding

problem.title: Reverse the Vowels in a String
problem.description: Implement a function that reverses only the vowels in a string while keeping consonants and spaces in their original positions.
requirements: Identify all vowels in the input string (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive)
Reverse the order of only the vowels
Keep all consonants and spaces in their original positions
Handle strings with no vowels or single vowel
Return the modified string
hints: Use two pointers/indices to find vowels from the start and end
Create a helper function to check if a character is a vowel (case-insensitive)
Convert the string to a rune slice for easier character manipulation

problem.title: Word Frequency Counter
problem.description: Write a function that analyzes a string and returns how many times each word appears. The function should be case-insensitive and handle punctuation.
requirements: Function returns an empty map when given an empty string
Function counts single and multiple different words
Function correctly counts repeated words with their frequency
Function is case-insensitive (treats 'Hello' and 'hello' as the same word)
Function strips common punctuation (.,!?;:) from words
Function handles multiple consecutive spaces correctly
hints: Use strings.Fields() to split text by whitespace
Use strings.ToLower() to normalize words to lowercase
Use strings.Trim() with strings.ContainsAny() to remove punctuation
Use a map[string]int to store and increment word frequencies

problem.title: Shopping Cart with Bulk Discounts
problem.description: Implement a shopping cart system that calculates totals with support for bulk discounts, promotional codes, and tax calculation. The cart should maintain line items and apply discounts based on quantity or promotional codes.
requirements: Add items to cart with item name, quantity, and per-unit price
Calculate subtotal as sum of (quantity × price) for all items in cart
Apply bulk discounts based on quantity thresholds (e.g., 10% off when quantity ≥ 10 for that item)
Apply promotional code discounts to the entire order (e.g., 'SUMMER20' applies 20% off)
Calculate tax as a percentage of the discounted subtotal
Generate itemized receipt showing each line item, all discounts applied, subtotal, tax, and final total
hints: Start with a simple Item class to hold name, quantity, and price; build up from basic add and subtotal
Use a List or Map to store items; handle duplicate item names by updating quantity
Calculate bulk discount per item first, then apply promotional codes to the overall subtotal
Keep discount calculations separate from subtotal for easier testing and debugging
Consider storing promo codes with their discount percentages in a Map for validation

problem.title: String Calculator with Custom Delimiters
problem.description: Implement a calculator that sums numbers in a string, supporting multiple delimiter types and custom delimiter definitions. Handle edge cases like negative numbers and numbers exceeding a threshold.
requirements: Return 0 for empty string input
Sum comma-separated numbers (e.g., "1,2,3" returns 6)
Support newline as an additional delimiter alongside commas

Support custom single-character delimiters via header syntax (e.g., "//;
1;2;3" returns 6 using semicolon)
Throw IllegalArgumentException if any negative number is present in the input
Ignore any numbers greater than or equal to 1000 in the sum calculation
hints: Start with the simplest cases first (empty string, single number) before adding delimiter complexity
Use regular expressions or String.split() to handle multiple delimiter types
Parse the custom delimiter header (//X\n format) before processing the number list
Keep the parsing logic separate from the summation logic for cleaner code and easier testing
